Hi Daniela — thanks again for the call earlier today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap (what we discussed)
- FinaPro wants a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood for inference: customer-managed VPC with model-serving in private subnets.
- Key concerns: PII handling, data retention and log retention windows, strict egress controls (no unexpected outbound connections), and a potential on-prem/air-gapped deployment for a small pilot.
- Regulatory ask: keep production data within US regions and support integration with your KMS/HSM.

Clarifying questions for you (quick):
1) Do you have a preferred key management provider (AWS KMS vs. HSM vendor) or should we present both options?
2) For the pilot, is the expectation fully air-gapped (no outbound network) or limited managed egress to approved endpoints?
3) Target retention windows for request/response logs and model telemetry? (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days)

What Redwood will deliver next:
- A concise network/data flow diagram showing control plane vs. data plane boundaries and required VPC endpoints. (attachment: redwood-vpc-dataflow-diagram.png)
- A short security checklist mapping items to your SOC2/security questions and where we can provide artifacts. (attachment: redwood-security-reqs.pdf)
- A proposed time for a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Dev) to walk firewall rules, VPC endpoints, and possible air-gapped steps.

Proposed next steps / timing
- I’ll share the network diagram + checklist by tomorrow morning (PST).
- Can we book a 60-min technical session next week? I’m proposing Tue 2026-02-10, 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2026-02-11, 14:00–15:00 PT. Please let me know what works for you.

Thanks — will prioritize the diagram based on your answers to the clarifying questions above.

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. A few items from our security/privacy side we need addressed before proceeding to a pilot: 

1) PII handling: we need documentation showing exactly where PII may be persisted (KV cache, logs, model-host disk) and the mechanisms to configure or disable persistence. Can Redwood guarantee that request/response payloads are never stored outside our VPC for the Private deployment?

2) Logging & retention: our security policy requires retention windows to be configurable and the ability to purge logs on request. Please confirm supported retention granularities (per-token auditing versus request-level) and whether we can opt out of telemetry collection.

3) Egress controls / network boundaries: for our compliance team, the requirement is that outbound traffic can be limited to specific private endpoints or blocked entirely. For an on-prem pilot we may require zero internet egress. Can you provide a concrete list of external endpoints Redwood needs for model updates, telemetry, or control plane operations and whether those can be disabled?

4) Key management: we require customer-managed keys. We use AWS KMS for cloud and Thales HSM for on-prem. Does Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM and support bring-your-own-keys where Redwood never has access to the plaintext key material?

5) Data residency: we need to confirm that model inference and any ephemeral storage will remain in our US tenancy and will not traverse EU/APAC regions.

If you can get answers and a diagram, the security team will do a quick triage. Also send the checklist mapping to SOC2 items so we can track open items. For scheduling, Tue 10am PT on 2026-02-10 works for me.

Thanks,

Daniela Ruiz
Head of Data Privacy & Compliance, FinaPro Analytics

Marissa / Dev — posting quick technical answers we should send to Daniela + security. I’ll also prepare a pared-down diagram for the security review.

Key points we should confirm in the reply: 
- Data plane locality: For Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC, inference containers (data plane) run entirely in the customer's account/VPC private subnets. No customer payloads leave the VPC unless explicitly configured (e.g., optional S3 model pulls or metrics endpoints).

- Persistence: By default, request/response payloads are ephemeral in memory. We persist only minimal telemetry required for billing and health by default — these can be disabled or configured. KV cache and any disk-backed caches can be configured to use ephemeral volumes or a customer-provided S3 with lifecycle rules. We can present config knobs: "persist_requests": true|false, "telemetry_level": none|basic|detailed, and retention_days: integer.

- Egress control: Options we support today:
  * Fully isolated (air-gapped) on-prem appliance: no outbound connections; model artifacts are provisioned via secure offline transfer.
  * Customer VPC private deployment with zero egress policy: uses VPC endpoints (S3 gateway endpoints or private ECR) for model artifacts, and blocks NAT gateway. Control plane can be optionally routed through a customer-controlled control plane in their account.
  * Standard Private: minimal outbound to Redwood control plane for orchestration (can be restricted to IP allowlist and mutual TLS).

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS via external key wrapping. For on-prem HSMs, we can integrate via PKCS#11 or bring a local keyserver; Redwood will not persist plaintext keys. Need to validate Thales specifics in follow-up.

- Logging & retention: We can provide request-level audit logs pushed to a customer-owned S3 bucket, with retention controlled by lifecycle policies. We can also implement a purge API to delete telemetry on demand; project expected dev effort is ~2 weeks to extend purge workflows for pilot.

Docs/Artifacts to attach: network diagram (will indicate required security groups, allowed CIDR endpoints, optional VPC endpoints), list of minimal outbound endpoints (IP ranges / FQDNs) for optional control plane services, and a short PII handling statement for Private deployments.

- Schedule the 60-min deep dive on Tue 2026-02-10 10:00–11:00 PT (hold a calendar + invite).

Hi Daniela + security team — attaching the diagram and checklist we discussed. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

Inline answers to your numbered items:
1) PII handling: In a Redwood Private deployment the inference path is confined to the customer VPC and data is processed in-memory. We can disable persisting request/response payloads entirely. KV cache persistence is configurable and can be placed on ephemeral volumes or your customer S3. See section A of the attached checklist for exact config toggles.

2) Logging & retention: Supported retention knobs: 0 (disabled), 7, 30, 90, 365 days. We can push audit logs to your S3 bucket (recommended) and implement a purge API for this pilot; ETA for purge API: ~10 business days to deliver and test.

3) Egress controls / network boundaries: Minimal external endpoints required only if you opt into Redwood-managed control plane:
  - control.redwood.ai (mTLS, optional, IP allowlist)
  - model-updates.redwood.ai (optional; can be replaced by customer-hosted model repository)
  All of these are optional and can be disabled for a zero-egress on-prem pilot. The attached network diagram shows the firewall rules we require if you keep a customer VPC-only setup.

4) Key management: We support AWS KMS BYOK and common enterprise HSMs (Thales, Gemalto) via PKCS#11 or KMIP bridges. Redwood will not store plaintext key material. We’ll follow up with a short integration checklist for Thales specifically.

5) Data residency: Confirmed — the Private deployment runs in your tenancy/VPC. No data leaves the region unless you explicitly enable cross-region replication for model artifacts.

Attachments included:
- redwood-vpc-dataflow-diagram.png — network boundaries, SGs, and optional VPC endpoints.
- redwood-security-reqs.pdf — security checklist mapped to common SOC2 items and our suggested configuration for the pilot.
